extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials and staff responsible for Section 504/accessibility compliance (program managers, accessibility coordinators, legal counsel), and applicants/recipients of agency programs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards agencies must follow to comply with Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (program accessibility, non‑discrimination, communications, complaint procedures, self‑evaluation, and special rules for historic properties, construction, and employment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical or mental impairment (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes anatomical loss affecting body systems (neurological; musculoskeletal; special sense organs; respiratory, including speech organs; cardiovascular; reproductive; digestive; genitourinary; hemic and lymphatic; skin; endocrine) and mental or psychological disorders such as mental retardation, organic brain syndrome, emotional or mental illness, and specific learning disabilities; includes diseases/conditions such as orthopedic, visual, speech, and hearing impairments, cerebral palsy, epilepsy, muscular dystrophy, multiple sclerosis, cancer, heart disease, diabetes, mental retardation, emotional illness, and drug addiction and alcoholism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is used to determine whether an individual has an impairment covered by the regulation; the list is illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major life activities (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Major life activities includes functions such as caring for one's self, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing, learning, and working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate whether an impairment substantially limits an individual's functioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has a record of such an impairment (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means has a history of, or has been misclassified as having, a mental or physical impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes coverage for individuals previously regarded as impaired even if they are not currently limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is regarded as having an impairment (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means (i) has an impairment that does not substantially limit major life activities but is treated by the agency as constituting such a limitation; (ii) has an impairment that substantially limits major life activities only as a result of the attitudes of others; or (iii) has none of the impairments defined but is treated by the agency as having such an impairment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers persons subject to discriminatory treatment based on perceived impairments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic preservation programs (definition and constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs conducted by the agency that have preservation of historic properties as a primary purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers special rules regarding accessibility and allowable alternatives where physical alteration would substantially impair significant historic features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic properties (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Properties that are listed or eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places or properties designated as historic under a statute of the appropriate State or local government body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the set of properties for which the historic‑preservation exceptions and priorities apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified handicapped person (definition and subcategories)
rubrics_metrics.description: For education services: a handicapped person who is a member of a class of persons otherwise entitled by statute, regulation, or policy to receive education services. For other programs requiring services/achievement: a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements and can achieve the purpose of the program without modifications that would result in a fundamental alteration. For any other program: a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements for participation in or receipt of benefits. For employment: defined by 29 CFR 1613.702(f) (made applicable by § 500.140).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes who is 'qualified' for protection; includes different tests depending on program type and references employment rules in EEOC regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 504 applicability to Executive agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this part, section 504 applies only to programs or activities conducted by Executive agencies and not to federally assisted programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits the scope of the regulation to federal agency‑conducted programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial impairment (historic properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a significant loss of the integrity of finished materials, design quality, or special character resulting from a permanent alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine when accessibility alterations would unacceptably impair historic properties and when alternative accommodations are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self‑evaluation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall, by August 24, 1987, evaluate its current policies and practices and the effects thereof that do not or may not meet the requirements of this part and, to the extent modification is required, proceed to make the necessary modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons and representative organizations) to participate via oral and written comments; maintain on file for three years a description of areas examined and problems identified and a description of modifications made, available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice obligation to inform covered persons
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall make available to employees, applicants, participants, beneficiaries, and other interested persons information regarding the provisions of this part and its applicability to the programs or activities conducted by the agency, and make such information available in such manner as the head of the agency finds necessary to apprise such persons of the protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must proactively inform stakeholders of their rights and the regulation's applicability; format and method determined by agency head.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibitions against discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific prohibitions when providing aid, benefit, or service: (i) deny opportunity to participate/benefit; (ii) afford unequal opportunity; (iii) provide aid/services not as effective in affording equal opportunity to obtain same result/benefit/achievement; (iv) provide different or separate aid/services unless necessary to provide equally effective aid; (v) deny opportunity to participate as member of planning/advisory boards; (vi) otherwise limit enjoyment of rights, privileges, advantages, or opportunities. Agencies must avoid both intentional discrimination and practices that have discriminatory effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑separate program participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not deny a qualified handicapped person the opportunity to participate in programs or activities that are not separate or different, despite the existence of permissibly separate or different programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes access to integrated programs where they exist even if separate programs are also offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discriminatory criteria and administration methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not, directly or through other arrangements, utilize criteria or methods of administration the purpose or effect of which would (i) subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap; or (ii) defeat or substantially impair accomplishment of the objectives of a program or activity with respect to handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative rules, selection criteria, or procedures must be evaluated for discriminatory purpose or effect and adjusted to prevent discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site selection non‑discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not, in determining the site or location of a facility, make selections the purpose or effect of which would (i) exclude handicapped persons from, deny them the benefits of, or otherwise subject them to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency; or (ii) defeat or substantially impair the accomplishment of the objectives of a program or activity with respect to handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Location decisions must consider accessibility and not have exclusionary effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement contractor selection criteria non‑discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency, in the selection of procurement contractors, may not use criteria that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting criteria must not result in discrimination by contractors delivering federally conducted services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and certification program administration limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not administer a licensing or certification program in a manner that subjects qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap, nor may the agency establish requirements for programs or activities of licensees or certified entities that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination; however, the programs of licensed or certified entities themselves are not covered by this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency licensing rules must avoid discriminatory burdens; coverage is limited to agency‑administered licensing/certification activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall administer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize placements and service delivery that integrate disabled persons with others to the maximum extent appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment non‑discrimination and procedural applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be subjected to discrimination in employment under any program or activity conducted by the agency; the definitions, requirements, and procedures of section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 791), as established by the EEOC in 29 CFR part 1613, shall apply to employment in federally conducted programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment complaints/processes follow EEOC/29 CFR part 1613 procedures as incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility — prohibition when facilities inaccessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided in § 500.150, no qualified handicapped person shall, because the agency's facilities are inaccessible to or unusable by handicapped persons, be denied the benefits of, be excluded from participation in, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inaccessibility of facilities cannot be a basis for exclusion; see § 500.150 for limited exceptions and compliance methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility for existing facilities (general obligation and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall operate each program or activity so that the program or activity, when viewed in its entirety, is readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons. This paragraph does not (1) necessarily require the agency to make each of its existing facilities accessible; (2) in historic preservation programs, require action that would result in substantial impairment of significant historic features; or (3) require action that would result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of a program or in undue financial and administrative burdens (agency bears burden of proving this and must document decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure overall program accessibility, may use alternatives where full structural access is not required, but must document and justify claims of fundamental alteration or undue burden and seek other measures to ensure benefits are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for achieving program accessibility (existing facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may comply through redesign of equipment, reassignment of services to accessible buildings, assignment of aides to beneficiaries, home visits, delivery of services at alternate accessible sites, alteration of existing facilities and construction of new facilities, use of accessible rolling stock, or any other methods that result in making its programs or activities readily accessible and usable by handicapped persons. The agency is not required to make structural changes where other methods are effective; in choosing methods, give priority to those that offer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit non‑exhaustive list of compliance options and directs priority to integrated solutions; structural alterations are not always required if alternatives achieve accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic preservation program accessibility methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In meeting accessibility requirements in historic preservation programs, the agency shall give priority to methods that provide physical access to handicapped persons. Where physical alteration is not required because of the historic preservation or fundamental alteration/undue burden exceptions, alternative methods include: (i) using audio‑visual materials and devices to depict portions that cannot be made accessible; (ii) assigning persons to guide handicapped persons into or through portions that cannot otherwise be made accessible; or (iii) adopting other innovative methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When historic features preclude alteration, agencies must prioritize physical access where possible and otherwise implement alternative accommodations that convey the experience or access by other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time periods for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall comply with obligations under § 500.150 by October 21, 1986, except that where structural changes are undertaken, such changes shall be made by August 22, 1989, but in any event as expeditiously as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines apply to program accessibility obligations; agencies must proceed promptly and within specified dates for structural work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural changes will be undertaken, the agency shall develop, by February 23, 1987, a transition plan setting forth the steps necessary to complete such changes. The agency shall provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons or representative organizations) to participate in developing the plan and must make the plan available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum the plan shall: (1) identify physical obstacles in facilities that limit accessibility; (2) describe in detail methods to make facilities accessible; (3) specify schedule for steps necessary to achieve compliance and annual steps if plan period >1 year; and (4) indicate the official responsible for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: New construction and alterations accessibility standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building or part of a building constructed or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of the agency shall be designed, constructed, or altered so as to be readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons. The definitions, requirements, and standards of the Architectural Barriers Act apply to buildings covered by this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New construction and alterations must meet Architectural Barriers Act standards (41 CFR 101‑19.600 to 101‑19.607); accessibility is required at the design and construction stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications — effective communication and auxiliary aids
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure effective communication with applicants, participants, personnel of other Federal entities, and members of the public. The agency shall furnish appropriate auxiliary aids where necessary to afford a handicapped person an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy the benefits of a program or activity. In determining what type of auxiliary aid is necessary, the agency shall give primary consideration to the requests of the handicapped person. The agency need not provide individually prescribed devices, readers for personal use or study, or other devices of a personal nature. Where the agency communicates by telephone, TDDs or equally effective telecommunications shall be used. The agency shall ensure persons with impaired vision or hearing can obtain information as to the existence and location of accessible services, and shall provide signage at a primary entrance directing users to where they can obtain information about accessible facilities and shall use the international symbol for accessibility at each primary entrance of an accessible facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must prioritize requested auxiliary aids, provide TDDs for telephone communications, ensure public information availability (including signage), and may claim fundamental alteration/undue burden defenses only with written justification and must seek alternative methods to the maximum extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for fundamental alteration or undue burden (communications and accessibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not require the agency to take any action that it can demonstrate would result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of a program or in undue financial and administrative burdens. Where agency personnel believe a proposed action would fundamentally alter the program or result in undue burdens, the agency has the burden of proving that compliance would result in such alteration or burdens. The decision must be made by the agency head or designee after considering all agency resources and must be accompanied by a written statement of reasons. If an action required to comply would result in such an alteration or burdens, the agency shall take any other action that would not result in such an alteration or burdens but would nevertheless ensure, to the maximum extent possible, handicapped persons receive the benefits and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict documentation and decision‑making standards apply before claiming exceptions; agencies must still identify and implement alternate measures where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance procedures — scope and processing of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: This section applies to all allegations of discrimination on the basis of handicap in programs or activities conducted by the agency except employment complaints processed per 29 CFR part 1613. The agency shall process complaints: accept and investigate all complete complaints for which it has jurisdiction; require that complete complaints be filed within 180 days of the alleged act (agency may extend for good cause); promptly notify complainants where the agency lacks jurisdiction and reasonably refer complaints to the appropriate entity; notify the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board upon receipt of complaints alleging inaccessible buildings subject to AB Act or section 502.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director coordinates implementation; within 180 days of receipt of a complete complaint the agency shall notify the complainant of results in a letter containing findings of fact and conclusions of law, a description of a remedy for each violation found, and notice of right to appeal. Appeals must be filed within 90 days (may be extended for good cause) and are processed by the head of the agency who must notify the complainant of results within 60 days (with a 60‑day period to decide once additional information is received). Time limits may be extended by the Assistant Attorney General. The agency may delegate authority to conduct investigations but may not delegate final determination authority to another agency.
